About us

Our team of skilled white hat hackers who are into top hackers list of Facebook, Uber, Twitter, Salesforce etc. penetrates into your applications/ network from a hacker’s perspective. 𝗔𝗻 𝗔𝗣𝗜 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗮 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿 𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀. The real risk often lies in the gaps between endpoints, permissions, and business logic. A user may access another user’s records, invoke a restricted function, or exploit a workflow that fails to enforce the right checks. Automated scanning helps identify common weaknesses, but finding an endpoint is not the same as validating an attack path. Manual testing adds the context needed to investigate authorisation flaws, trace related requests and confirm real-world impact. Our latest guide explains how API penetration testing moves beyond scanning to uncover exploitable risks, validate findings and verify fixes. #AppSecure #APISecurity #PenetrationTesting #Cybersecurity #AppSec #API #ApplicationSecurity

Known dependency CVEs and certain infrastructure misconfigurations have relatively deterministic fixes, making them strong candidates for automation. Application vulnerabilities are different. Business logic flaws, broken access control, injection and IDOR often require an understanding of the application's architecture and intended behaviour. The better approach is AI-assisted remediation: AI provides exploitation context and code-specific guidance, developers make informed remediation decisions, and automated testing verifies that fixes work without breaking existing functionality. AI should accelerate the remediation loop while keeping human judgement at the centre. #AppSecure #AppSec #AI #VulnerabilityManagement #PenetrationTesting #ApplicationSecurity

A vendor security questionnaire can tell you what a supplier says about its controls. It cannot tell you whether those controls withstand an actual attack. Third-party penetration testing provides a different kind of evidence. It tests defined vendor systems and integrations for exploitable weaknesses, validates real impact, and helps security teams make better risk decisions. But testing a third party is not simply a matter of running a scan. Scope, written authorisation, rules of engagement, production safeguards and ownership must be established before testing begins. Our latest guide explains how to approach third-party penetration testing, when it is appropriate, and how to use the findings within a broader vendor risk programme. #AppSecure #ThirdPartyRisk #PenetrationTesting #Cybersecurity #VendorRisk #AppSec #CyberRisk

An annual penetration test provides a point-in-time view of your security posture. It does not account for everything that changes between assessments. New releases, infrastructure changes, authentication updates and security incidents can all introduce new attack paths. That is why penetration testing frequency should be aligned with the risk, exposure and rate of change of each environment. High-risk customer-facing systems may require quarterly or continuous validation, while significant architectural or authentication changes can warrant testing outside the regular schedule. Our latest blog examines how organisations can build a penetration testing cadence that balances continuous security validation with compliance requirements. #AppSecure #PenetrationTesting #Cybersecurity #ApplicationSecurity #CyberRisk #SecurityTesting #Compliance

We walked through the product demo, AppSecure’s AI pentesting capabilities, and the classes of issues our agents actually look for. Then: 𝗖𝗮𝗻 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝘀𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗮 𝗰𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁? 𝗥𝗲𝗱𝗮𝗰𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗲. We said no. And offered to run AppSecure’s agent on a small app for free instead. The CISO pushed back: two other vendors had already sent redacted reports. We asked him to send those over. Not to copy them. To show how fast you can un-redact them. API paths. URI patterns. URL schemes. Error shapes. Business logic. Industry fingerprints. Enough of that survives “redaction” that you can often name the company. If those vendors are handing their clients’ reports to you, yours can walk out the same door. That landed. He signed. Redaction is not confidentiality. A report is a map of someone’s systems. Treat it like one. #agentic_pentest #appsecure

For enterprise SaaS, the real attack surface extends across APIs, identity, tenant boundaries, cloud infrastructure, integrations, and business logic. A scanner can identify known vulnerability classes. It cannot reliably determine whether Tenant A can access Tenant B’s data, whether a multi-step workflow can be abused, or whether several weaknesses can be chained into a meaningful attack path. That distinction matters when enterprise buyers, auditors, and security teams are evaluating whether your platform is actually secure. A strong application security assessment should answer a harder question: What could an attacker actually do with the weaknesses across the platform? That means testing the full attack surface, validating real attack paths, remediating findings, and retesting what was fixed. #AppSecure #ApplicationSecurity #SaaSSecurity #Cybersecurity #PenetrationTesting #AppSec #EnterpriseSaaS

Authentication confirms who you are. Authorisation determines what you can access. If changing an object ID lets one user access another user’s invoice, document, order, or record, the API has an authorisation gap. Finding these flaws takes more than scanning endpoints. Testers need to work across identities, swap object IDs, test different HTTP methods, and validate access across roles and tenants. Our latest guide breaks down how to test API1:2023 BOLA and where automated scanning falls short. #AppSecure #APISecurity #BOLA #PenetrationTesting #Cybersecurity #AppSec #API

Choosing an external penetration testing provider for an audit is not simply about finding someone who can run a test. The real question is whether the engagement produces evidence your auditor can actually use. Manual testing depth, framework mapping, tester credentials, reporting quality, and retesting all matter. So does understanding the attack surface your industry operates in. A PTaaS platform may make sense when you need continuous testing. A CREST-accredited firm may be the right choice when accreditation is explicitly required. A large consultancy may fit broader governance needs. But when the goal is a compliance-ready external penetration test, the provider needs to match the framework, scope, and evidence requirements not just the budget. We compared the major types of external penetration testing providers and where each one fits best. #AppSecure #PenetrationTesting #Cybersecurity #Compliance #SecurityAudits #AppSec #CyberRisk

A standard SaaS pentest can tell you whether the application is secure. But what happens when the application can reason over privileged client data? For legal tech, adding AI changes the attack surface. A drafting assistant, research copilot, or document workflow can introduce new paths to sensitive matters through prompt injection, retrieval boundaries, access-control failures, and integrations. The risk is not simply that the AI produces a bad answer. It is that the AI becomes a new way to reach something the user was never authorized to see. Our latest blog looks at AI penetration testing for legal tech, what needs to be tested, where security teams should focus, and what to look for when evaluating a testing provider. #AppSecure #LegalTech #AISecurity #AIPenetrationTesting #Cybersecurity #AppSec
